item.title: How to get follow-up off the founder's calendar
item.description: Follow-up that lives on the founder's calendar is not a system. Sequences, a same-day first reply, and a next step written in the CRM are. If you are the glue, the glue dries when you travel.

item.title: How to make CRM ownership visible
item.description: CRM ownership is visible when one named person is responsible for the next step on every open deal, and you can see that step without asking. A CRM nobody updates is a filing cabinet with a login.

How to run a Decision Cost Audit
item.description: A Decision Cost Audit is not a software demo. I sit with one workflow lane, inventory the recurring decisions, force Automate / Assist / Keep Human, then we implement one quick win and measure it. AI can draft. I lock the call. If nobody signs off, it does not ship.

item.title: What is the Decision Cost Framework
item.description: The Decision Cost Framework is my original method for a question I kept hitting in sales ops: what does it cost to keep deciding this by hand? Decision Cost is the organizational cost of using human judgment to start, approve, prioritize, interpret, escalate, or authorize work when Automate, Assist, or Keep Human would be a better split. It is not all labor. The unit is a Decision Episode. v0.1. Declared. Not certified.

what is the decision cost framework 3
Why a booking link does not fix no-shows
item.description: A booking link captures a time. It does not recover a no-show. Reminders, a same-day ping, and a named owner for the reschedule are the actual job. I have watched operators add a prettier Cal.com page and still lose the week to empty Zoom rooms.
